content.value_statement: Phylogenetic biogeography workflows often fail because tree labels, distribution files, and model settings do not align. This skill validates inputs and prepares a reproducible BioGeoBEARS analysis with comparisons and visualizations.
actual_capabilities: Validates PHYLIP-like geography files, binary range codes, area counts, and species counts.
Checks geography species names against tip labels parsed from a Newick tree.
Reformats CSV or TSV presence data into the format required by BioGeoBEARS.
Prepares an RMarkdown workflow for DEC, DIVALIKE, BAYAREALIKE, and selected +J variants.
Compares fitted models using likelihoods, AIC, AICc, AIC weights, and paired likelihood-ratio summaries.
Produces saved model objects, ancestral-range PDF plots, an HTML report, and session information.
limitations: Requires R 4.0 or later, BioGeoBEARS dependencies, RMarkdown packages, and Python 3.
Input trees must be rooted, include branch lengths, and use labels matching the geography file.
Runtime grows quickly as area count, maximum range size, and tree size increase.
Model selection and +J interpretation require biological justification and current statistical guidance.

use_cases.title: Prepare an island clade study
use_cases.description: Validate a tree and island-presence table before reconstructing ancestral ranges.

use_cases.title: Standardize collaborative inputs
use_cases.description: Convert mixed CSV or TSV distribution data into a consistent BioGeoBEARS geography file.

use_cases.title: Compare biogeographic models
use_cases.description: Prepare a documented workflow that compares model fit and produces plots for a thesis.

prompt_templates.title: Validate analysis inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate [tree path] and [geography path]. Report rooting, branch-length, label, delimiter, and binary-code problems before changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with an existing tree and geography file.

prompt_templates.title: Reformat distribution data
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert [distribution path] into BioGeoBEARS geography format. Preserve the source, list normalized species names, and validate against [tree path].
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare CSV or TSV presence data.

prompt_templates.title: Configure model comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an analysis for [tree path] and [geography path] using maximum range size [number]. Compare [models] and generate both plot types.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose and interpret results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [report path] and [results directory]. Identify convergence concerns, compare supported models, explain parameter uncertainty, and state interpretation limits.

output_examples.input: Validate a rooted 30-tip bird tree against a five-island distribution table.
output: The tree contains 30 tips and branch lengths.
Two geography labels do not match tree tips.
The area count and binary-code lengths are consistent.

output_examples.input: Prepare a workspace comparing DEC, DEC+J, DIVALIKE, and DIVALIKE+J.
output_examples.output: A documented analysis workspace contains validated inputs, a parameterized RMarkdown report, model-result storage, and ancestral-range plot directories.

output: Models are ranked by AIC with likelihoods, parameter counts, and AIC weights.
The summary highlights convergence concerns and avoids treating one statistic as biological proof.

best_practices: Keep original inputs unchanged and write normalized copies into a dedicated analysis directory.
Choose maximum range size from biological evidence because state space and runtime grow quickly.
Review convergence, parameter estimates, and model assumptions before interpreting AIC rankings.
anti_patterns: Do not continue when tree tips and geography species names differ.
Do not set maximum range size only to reduce runtime without biological justification.
Do not interpret +J support as definitive evidence without checking assumptions and current methodological guidance.

faq.question: Which input formats are supported?
faq.answer: Trees use Newick format. Geography data can be PHYLIP-like text, CSV, or TSV presence tables.

faq.question: Does the skill install BioGeoBEARS?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation requirements and commands, but package installation remains user-managed.

faq.question: Can it repair species-name mismatches automatically?
faq.answer: It identifies mismatches and normalizes spaces during reformatting. Users should approve biological name changes or taxon removal.

faq.question: Which models can the template compare?
faq.answer: The template supports DEC, DIVALIKE, BAYAREALIKE, and selected variants with founder-event parameter J.

faq.question: What outputs does the workflow produce?
faq.answer: It produces an HTML report, saved R model objects, ancestral-range PDF plots, model tables, and session information.

faq.question: Is the workflow suitable for large datasets?
faq.answer: Yes, but many areas, broad range sizes, and large trees can require substantial memory and runtime.
